questions.question: In an RTK Query `onCacheEntryAdded` handler, why do you `await cacheDataLoaded` before applying socket messages?
options: So deltas are applied on top of the fetched snapshot instead of to a cache entry that has no data yet
Because WebSockets cannot open before a query finishes
To make the socket reconnect automatically
It is required for TypeScript inference only
questions.explanation: The recipe is snapshot first, then deltas. updateCachedData needs existing data to patch, so you wait for the initial query to resolve.

questions.question: Two components both call `useGetNavsQuery()` for a streaming endpoint. How many WebSocket connections are opened?
options: One, because onCacheEntryAdded runs once per cache entry, shared by all subscribers
Zero until one of them calls refetch
questions.explanation: onCacheEntryAdded runs when the cache entry is created and its cleanup runs when the last subscriber leaves, so all subscribers share one connection.

questions.question: What does marking an action with `prepareAutoBatched()` change?
options: The reducer runs later, at the end of the frame
The action is sent to the server in a batch
The state updates immediately, but subscriber notifications are delayed and coalesced
questions.explanation: The autoBatchEnhancer (on by default in configureStore) keeps state current but delays notifying subscribers, so many fast actions cause one notification.

questions.question: Why should each queued offline write carry a unique ID sent to the server?
options: Redux requires every action to have an id
So the entity adapter can store it
As an idempotency key, so a retried request after a timeout is not applied twice
questions.explanation: A request may succeed on the server even though the client saw a timeout. An idempotency key lets the server ignore the duplicate retry.
